articles.title: Pubill no olvida la eliminación ante el Arsenal: “Me celebró en la cara”
articles.standfirst: El defensa del Atlético admite que terminó molesto tras la eliminatoria y evita profundizar en la polémica con los jugadores 'gunners'
articles.summary: El defensa del Atlético admite que terminó molesto tras la eliminatoria y evita profundizar en la polémica con los jugadores 'gunners'
articles.body: Marc Pubill dejó una de las declaraciones más llamativas de su entrevista en Radio MARCA al recordar la reciente eliminatoria contra el Arsenal. El lateral rojiblanco reconoció que acabó especialmente enfadado por la actitud de un rival tras el pitido final y que el episodio todavía sigue reciente. Durante la conversación, el internacional español explicó el origen de su enfado: "Gyokeres me lo celebró en la cara cuando pitó el árbitro al final”, aseguró el futbolista, dejando claro que no le sentó bien la reacción de uno de los jugadores del conjunto londinense. Aunque admitió su malestar, Pubill evitó alimentar la polémica. Cuando fue invitado a profundizar en lo ocurrido, optó por frenar la conversación en el momento en el que mencionaron a Merino y a Zubimendi: “No lo hemos hablado y no quiero hablarlo porque si no...”, respondió, dejando entrever que sigue considerando desafortunado aquel episodio. El defensa también confirmó que no ha comentado lo sucedido con los futbolistas del Arsenal con los que coincide actualmente en otros contextos competitivos. Su prioridad, explicó, es mantenerse centrado en el presente. Pese al recuerdo amargo de la eliminación, Pubill dejó claro que prefiere mirar hacia adelante. Fiel a la actitud positiva que ha mostrado durante toda la entrevista, el jugador mantiene el foco en los próximos retos y evita recrearse en una eliminatoria que todavía escuece en el vestuario rojiblanco.

articles.title: La UEFA no continuará con la 'Ley Vinicius'
articles.standfirst: El organismo europeo defiende que dicha medida limita la libertad de expresión de los jugadores
articles.summary: El organismo europeo defiende que dicha medida limita la libertad de expresión de los jugadores
articles.body: La llamada 'Ley Vinicius' ha dado mucho de qué hablar en esta edición del Mundial. Ya son dos los jugadores que han sido expulsados por esta medida: Miguel Almirón fue la primera víctima e Hincapié la más reciente, tras una discusión con el mexicano Santi Giménez. Cada vez que suceden estos episodios, la polémica se convierte en el centro de atención. Sin embargo, la UEFA ha confirmado que no aplicará dicha norma en sus competiciones, rechazando así la medida de la FIFA para la cita mundialista. El 'caso Vinicius-Prestianni' ha marcado un antes y un después en el reglamento del fútbol mundial. Es por ello que la FIFA ha querido adoptar esta norma, entre otras medidas innovadoras que buscan reducir la pérdida de tiempo, para que no se repitan episodios como el ocurrido en la Champions League durante el partido entre el Real Madrid y el Oporto. No obstante, los jugadores que decidan taparse la boca en la Champions y en las diferentes competiciones de la UEFA no serán expulsados. El organismo europeo ha optado por desmarcarse de la regla porque defiende que limita la libertad de expresión de los futbolistas. Esto revela un capítulo más del pulso entre el organismo de Gianni Infantino y el de Aleksander Ceferin, quienes toman caminos diferentes en varios aspectos, sobre todo en los relacionados con la materia arbitral.

articles.title: La Champions 26-27 se pone en marcha en pleno Mundial
articles.standfirst: Los primeros 28 equipos arrancan la primera ronda de clasificación
articles.summary: Los primeros 28 equipos arrancan la primera ronda de clasificación
articles.body: El Mundial 2026 está entrando en su fase decisiva. Pero, en medio toda esta vorágine, la Champions League 26-27 se pone en marcha desde hoy mismo. Un total de 83 equipos repartidos entre 53 de las 55 federaciones miembro de la UEFA participarán en esta edición de la Liga de Campeones con el objetivo de suceder al PSG y levantar la 'Orejona' en el Metropolitano, que acogerá su segunda final, el próximo 5 de junio de 2027. Su entrada en la competición, eso sí, se realizará de forma progresiva. En esta primera fase, participarán 28 equipos. Según los criterios que establece la competición, 12 derrotados se irán a la segunda ronda de clasificación de la Conference League, mientras que el perdedor de las eliminatorias 4 (Lincoln vs Inter Club d'Escaldes) y 5 (Tre Fiori vs Larne) irán a la tercera fase por cuestiones organizativas. Ya desde esta primera ronda de la Champions vamos a tener representación española. Tras el excelente trabajo de Bezares en el Lincoln, Ahora ha sido Juanma Pavón quien ha recogido su testigo... mientras que Julio Velázquez tratará de llevar a lo más alto al Levski Sofia después de poner fin a 14 años de tiranía por parte del Ludogorets en Bulgaria. El equipo con más cartel en esta primera fase de la Champions, sin embargo, es el Kairat Almaty. Situados en la frontera con China, ya debutaron en la competición —jugaron contra el Real Madrid— en la pasada edición... aunque apenas lograron sumar un punto contra el Pafos en la tercera jornada. Podrán contar, al menos hasta el próximo mes de agosto, con el prometedor Dastan Satpaev, quien ya ha sido fichado por el Chelsea. Su principal competencia en la punta de lanza es Marc Gual, ex de Sevilla, Girona o Alcorcón que se ha incorporado al Kairat desde el Río Ave como agente libre. En cinco partidos, ya suma un gol y dos asistencias. Las eliminatorias se disputarán a ida y vuelta y los 14 clasificados avanzarán a una segunda ronda donde ya se ubican equipos de la altura de Dinamo Zagreb, Estrella Roja o Slovan Bratislava. Fenerbahçe, Górnik Zabrze, Sturm Graz y Hearts también arrancarán desde la Ruta de Liga. Aquí arranca la Champions.

articles.title: La Champions 26-27 echa a rodar... con marcado acento español
articles.standfirst: Se disputaron los 10 primeros partidos de la primera ronda previa
articles.summary: Se disputaron los 10 primeros partidos de la primera ronda previa
articles.body: Ya han finalizado los octavos de final y el Mundial 2026 entra en su fase decisiva. Pero, mientras termina de definirse, la Champions 26-27 ya se ha puesto en marcha con la disputa de los primeros partidos de la primera ronda previa. Aquí inicia el camino a la final que tendrá lugar en el Metropolitano el próximo 5 de junio. Ya desde el inicio de la competición, hubo marcado acento español. El Lincoln de Juan Manuel Pavón entró con buen pie y sacó un gran resultado en Gibraltar frente al Inter Club d'Escaldes (3-1), donde milita el hijo de Mauricio Pochettino, de cara al encuentro de vuelta que se disputará en Andorra. Julio Velázquez y su Levski Sofía, por su parte, acabaron rescatando un valioso empate contra el Borac (1-1) en tierras bosnias. Todo se puso en contra con el tanto de penalti transformado por Juricic a los nueve minutos de encuentro. Pero, nada más arrancar la segunda parte, Oko-Flex devolvió la igualdad al marcador. Fue el único empate del día junto al del Kauno Zalgiris frente al Drita. Fue, también, una primera tanda de partidos marcada por las tarjetas rojas. De hecho, hubo hasta cuatro expulsiones repartidas por las derrotas del Riga, Vardar y Shamrock Rovers. El Sabah, por su parte, sí sacó su encuentro adelante frente al The New Saints (2-0)... a pesar de disputar los últimos minutos con uno menos. La gran alegría de la tarde-noche de Champions se la llevó el Vikingur gracias a su victoria sobre la bocina frente al Gyor. Mañana, será turno para un Kairat Almaty que ya estuvo presente en la pasada edición de Champions. Reciben en casa al Sutjeska. Cierran la jornada Flora vs. Iberia; Petrocub vs. Egnatia; y Vitebsk vs. Universitatea.

articles.title: Marc Gual vuelve a ilusionar al Kairat Almaty con la Champions
articles.standfirst: El español anotó un gol en las instancias finales para darle la victoria al conjunto uzbeko en la ida de la primera fase previa del torneo
articles.summary: El atacante español anotó un gol en las instancias finales para darle la victoria al conjunto uzbeko
articles.body: El Kairat Almaty sigue soñando con la Champions League. El conjunto uzbeko, que fue una de las sorpresas de la competición europea la temporada pasada, está luchando en la fase previa para volver a meterse en la edición de esta campaña y de momento va en buen camino...gracias a un jugador español. Marc Gual anotó el gol que desequilibró el encuentro ante el Sutjeska macedonio en el encuentro de ida de la primera fase de clasificación. Tras un duelo igualado entre ambos conjuntos, un gol con el pecho de Lucas Áfrico en el minuto 76 dio la ventaja inicial al equipo uzbeko. Sin embargo, Marko Mrvaljevic igualó la contienda en el minuto 90, tras una asistencia de su centrocampista Deni Hocko. Cuando todo indicaba que el Sutjeska se marcharía con un empate de vuelta a Macedonia, allí emergió Marc Gual. El atacante español aprovechó un centro desde la banda derecha y el posterior salto de Edmilson para dejar pasar el balón para batir al guardameta macedonio. El camino para jugar la Champions es muy largo. El Kairat todavía tiene que ganar el segundo encuentro y tres rondas a ida y vuelta más para jugar la clasificación final. La temporada pasada lo consiguió, al imponerse de manera heroica a todo un histórico como el Celtic de Glasgow. A ver qué tal se le da en esta.

El atacante español aprovechó un centro desde la banda derecha y el posterior salto de Edmilson para dejar pasar el balón para batir al guardameta macedonio. El camino para jugar la Champions es muy largo. El Kairat todavía tiene que ganar el segundo encuentro y tres rondas a ida y vuelta más para jugar la clasificación final. La temporada pasada lo consiguió, al imponerse de manera heroica a todo un histórico como el Celtic de Glasgow. A ver qué tal se le da en esta.

articles.title: British South Asians in Football Team of the Season 2025/26: Hamza Choudhury, Zidane Iqbal, Yan Dhanda, Mariam Mahmood all feature
articles.summary: Sky Sports News' Dev Trehan and Desi Ballers founder Zohaib Rashid pick the fourth annual combined XI, celebrating the on-field contribution made by British South Asians in football during the 2025/2026 season
articles.body:
It has been another breakthrough campaign for British South Asians in football, but who makes it into the 2025/26 Team of the Season?

Players from the community featured across the leagues in men's football and at every level of the English women's football pyramid.

  • Transfer Centre LIVE! | Key dates for summer window 2026
  • Premier League ins and outs | Papers - latest headlines
  • Download the Sky Sports app and follow your club

Nine players retain their places from last year, but how does the overrall 2025/26 team shape up?

Goalkeeper

Jasbir Singh continued to lead from the back as Tamworth vice-captain, keeping eight clean sheets across the campaign and helping the Lambs claim a top-half finish in the 2025/26 National League.

Defenders

Asmita Ale makes her fourth consecutive Team of the Season appearance after a solid individual campaign. Ale played 21 Women's Super League matches across the season for Leicester City.

Danny Batth rolled back the years to play an important role for unfancied Derby County last season as the club narrowly missed out on the play-offs on the last day of the season, finishing eighth in the Sky Bet Championship.

Kam Kandola had the most productive season of his career to date, playing 38 matches in a campaign where Kidderminster Harriers clinched promotion to the National League via the play-offs. Kandola has joined Hereford ahead of the new season.

Mal Benning regained his place in Shrewsbury Town's line-up after the mid-season appointment of Gavin Cowan. Benning went on to make his 500th professional career appearance and helped the club preserve its League Two status.

Midfielders

Millie Chandarana became an 'Invincible' for the second consecutive season, featuring prominently as Burnley went unbeaten in the league to land the title and earn promotion to Women's Super League 2. Chandarana has just signed a new deal.

Hamza Choudhury played 32 matches for Leicester City in a difficult league campaign for the Foxes but sparkled on the international stage, scoring on his home debut for Bangladesh and instantly becoming a national hero.

Zidane Iqbal appeared in the Dutch Eredivisie and the Europa League for FC Utrecht in a season where he scored his first international goal and became the first British South Asian ever to play at a World Cup, featuring in all three of Iraq's games over the summer.

Forwards

Yan Dhanda emerged as a key player for Dundee following his loan switch from Hearts, featuring in 31 matches for the club and helping the Dee comfortably retain their place in the Scottish Premiership next season.

Mariam Mahmood had a fairytale season as she made her international debut for Pakistan ahead of clinching a move to Wrexham. The club won a historic league and cup double as Mahmood became the first Pakistani female to win a top-division European title.

Dilan Markanday landed a club end-of-season Player of the Year award after scoring eight goals and contributing six assists in a season where Chesterfield narrowly missed out on a League Two play-off spot.

articles.title: Juan Manuel Pavón y Julio Velázquez se apuntan otra ronda de Champions
articles.standfirst: Lincoln y Levski Sofía superaron la primera ronda de la Liga de Campeones
articles.summary: Lincoln y Levski Sofía superaron la primera ronda de la Liga de Campeones
articles.body: No sólo la Selección está de enhorabuena tras lograr el pase a la final del Mundial 2026. A los mandos del Lincoln y el Levski Sofía, respectivamente, Juan Manuel Pavón y Julio Velázquez se han apuntado a otra ronda de Champions con el sueño de estar entre los 36 que compondrán la fase liga de 36 definitiva. El Lincoln no pudo pasar del empate a su paso por Andorra para medirse al Inter Club d'Escaldes. Sin embargo, hicieron valer el 3-1 del choque de ida disputado en Gibraltar para plantarse en la segunda ronda previa, donde se toparán con un Kauno Zalgiris que repitió triunfo frente al Drita y avanzó con un 3-4 global en el marcador. El Levski Sofía, por su parte, venía de empatar frente el Borac y su fue con 0-0 al descanso. Pero, a partir de ahí, no dieron opción alguna y aplastaron en la segunda mitad con los goles de Oko-Flex, que ya 'mojó' en el partido de ida, el doblete de Reinaldo y otro tanto de Perea en los instantes finales. Su rival en la segunda ronda previa de esta Champions saldrá del ganador del choque entre el Universitatea Craiova, que goleó (1-4) en el encuentro de ida, o el ML Vitebsk. También quedan para mañana el Bissen-Klaksvík (1-2); Sutjeska-Kairat (1-2); y Egnatia-Petrocub (1-1).

articles.title: Marc Gual enciende la Champions: "Está difícil, pero lo vamos a intentar"
articles.standfirst: El '9' español suma cuatro goles y dos asistencias en seis partidos con el Kairat
articles.summary: El '9' español suma cuatro goles y dos asistencias en seis partidos con el Kairat
articles.body: El Kairat dio la sorpresa la temporada pasada clasificándose para la Champions League por primera vez en su historia. Una misión (casi) imposible que aspira a reeditar gracias a los goles de Marc Gual (Badalona, 1996). "Venía de no jugar demasiado en el Río Ave, recibí varias ofertas y, tras hablar con varios compañeros que ya conocía, me decanté por la del Kairat. Es un club que lucha por títulos y por competir en Europa, que cuenta con muy buenas instalaciones y la propuesta económica también era buena. Todo era positivo, así que decidí probar y, por ahora, la verdad es que todo va muy bien", asegura a MARCA. Los 8.000 kilómetros que separan Almaty de España parecían la principal barrera: "El tema de la distancia era lo que más me tiraba para atrás. El viaje, con los dos perros, se nos hizo un poco largo a mí y a mi mujer, pero es lo único malo. Almaty es una ciudad muy 'top': moderna, bien comunicada... Tiene de todo y se vive muy bien. Hemos acertado".  Sin embargo, el exatacante de Espanyol 'B', Sevilla Atlético, Zaragoza, Girona, Real Madrid Castilla, Alcorcón, Dnipro-1, Jagiellonia Bialystok, Legia y Río Ave ha caído de pie en el Kairat: acumula cuatro goles y dos asistencias en seis partidos.  "Hasta el momento está yendo todo muy bien. He marcado goles, he repartido asistencias y, desde que llegué, no hemos perdido. El estilo de juego me viene bien: queremos tener el balón, atacar mucho, crear ocasiones...", subraya Marc Gual antes de ahondar en las exigencias tácticas de Rafael Urazbakhtin: "El míster me pide es que aparezca entre líneas para crear ocasiones y en zonas de finalización para rematarlas. Ése es mi fuerte y para lo que estoy aquí".  Marcó, también, en la victoria por 2-1 sobre el Sutjeska Niksic montenegrino en la primera ronda previa de la 'vieja' Copa de Europa. "Entrar en Champions está difícil. La temporada pasada lo consiguieron por primera vez en su historia, pero lo normal es no conseguirlo porque el nivel es muy alto y tenemos que pasar cuatro rondas previas".  La posibilidad de perpetrar un nuevo milagro, sin embargo, está ahí: "Lo vamos a intentar. Ojalá pasemos esta primera ronda para asegurarnos entrar en Europa, aunque no sea Champions, pero jugar, al menos, la Europa Legue o la Conference. Vamos paso a paso y ya llegará lo que tenga que llegar", confiesa Marc Gual, que ya compitió en el Viejo Continente con el Legia. Con el Legia, precisamente, batió su récord anotador: marcó 19 goles en la 2024-25. No va por mal camino... pero no quiere desviar el tiro. "Siempre uno quiere marcar goles, pero lo principal es ayudar al equipo, jugar, tener minutos... El resto, si el equipo va bien, irá viniendo. Ojalá pueda superar los 19 goles que marque con el Legia, pero prefiero ganar la Liga y jugar en Europa que superar mi propio récord".  Hoy, nuevamente, les espera el Sutjeska Niksic. "Los partidos de Europa y de la Liga son diferentes. En la Liga somos el equipo grande, dominamos el juego y creamos ocasiones. En Europa los partidos son más igualados y los rivales más fuertes. Hay equipos que te dominan, algo que en la Liga no pasa tan a menudo. Tenemos que adaptarnos. Eso es lo que hará que podamos entrar en Europa", reconoce el '9' español del Kairat. Con Marc 'Goal' será más fácil.

articles.title: Marc Gual y el Kairat quieren volver a estar en Champions
articles.standfirst: El conjunto kazajo selló el pase a la segunda ronda de clasificación contra el Sutjeska
articles.summary: El conjunto kazajo selló el pase a la segunda ronda de clasificación contra el Sutjeska
articles.body: El Kairat ya hizo historia la temporada pasada al convertirse en el segundo equipo kazajo en disputar la Champions tras el Astana en 2015. Sin embargo, no se conforman con ello y están dispuestos a pasearse de nuevo por los mejores campos del Viejo Continente. Un gol del ariete español Marc Gual en el tiempo de descuento amarró el triunfo contra Sutjeska en el partido de ida. "Entrar en Champions está difícil. La temporada pasada lo consiguieron por primera vez en su historia, pero lo normal es no conseguirlo porque el nivel es muy alto y tenemos que pasar cuatro rondas previas", repasaba en MARCA el ex de Río Ave en la previa del choque de vuelta. De nuevo, Rafael Urazbakhtin lo ubicó como principal referencia en el Kairat. Sin embargo, fue el jovencísimo Ismail Bakbolat (2008) quien anotó el 0-1 justo antes de abandonar el campo. El Sutjeska estaba contra las cuerdas... y firmó su sentencia con la expulsión de Raznatovic y posterior tanto de penalti de Jorginho terminaron de amarrar el pase. En la siguiente ronda ya espera el Omonisa Nicosia en el tortuoso camino que le restan a Marc Gual y el Kairat hasta poder plantarse en la fase liga definitiva de la Champions 26-27. También sellaron la clasificación el Universitatea Craiova Rumanía), el Klakvik (Islas Feroe) y el Egnatia (Albania).

articles.title: El delantero español que quiere volver a hacer historia en la Champions: "Aquí solo vale ganar"
articles.standfirst: Marc Gual, reciente fichaje del Kairat Almaty kazajo, habla de su nueva vida en Marcador Internacional de Radio MARCA
articles.summary: Marc Gual, reciente fichaje del Kairat Almaty kazajo, habla de su nueva vida en Marcador Internacional de Radio MARCA
articles.body: Marc Gual ha iniciado una nueva etapa lejos del fútbol español. El delantero catalán, de 30 años, ha fichado este verano por el Kairat Almaty, vigente campeón de Kazajistán y uno de los clubes habituales en las rondas previas de la Liga de Campeones. En una entrevista concedida a Radio MARCA en el programa Marcador Internacional, el atacante explicó los motivos que le llevaron a aceptar una aventura "desconocida", aunque reconoce que el crecimiento del club en Europa terminó de convencerle. "El año pasado no fue el mejor que he tenido, jugué menos de lo que deseaba y había que cambiar de aires. Salió esta oportunidad y nos cuadró todo. Es un equipo que pelea por títulos y que puede jugar competiciones europeas", explicó Gual, que la pasada temporada militó en el Rio Ave portugués. Su estreno no ha podido ser mejor. El Kairat ya ha superado la primera eliminatoria previa de la Champions tras eliminar al Sutjeska, con un gol decisivo del propio delantero español en el encuentro de ida. Ahora espera el Omonia de Nicosia, un rival de mayor entidad en el camino hacia la fase de liga. "Sabemos que repetir lo del año pasado es muy complicado, pero si vamos partido a partido siempre es posible. El Omonia será un rival difícil, aunque creo que tenemos equipo para competir e intentar volver a entrar en la Champions", señaló. El Kairat adquirió notoriedad internacional la pasada temporada al convertirse en el primer club kazajo en disputar la fase de liga de la Champions, donde incluso recibió la visita del Real Madrid. Aquella histórica participación ha cambiado la dimensión del club. "Los compañeros que estuvieron el año pasado dicen que todo ha cambiado. La gente te reconoce por la calle porque juegas en el Kairat y el club ha crecido muchísimo gracias a esa participación europea. Eso sí, la presión aquí no es como en otros países", reconoció. Porque, según explica Gual, la verdadera exigencia está en el campeonato doméstico. "El objetivo principal es ganar la Liga. El Kairat ha conquistado las dos últimas y es el club grande del país. Eso es lo que te permite volver a jugar las previas de la Champions". Más allá del fútbol, el delantero también habló de su adaptación a Kazajistán, un cambio radical tanto por la distancia como por la cultura. Se ha trasladado a Almaty junto a su mujer y sus dos perros, una decisión que no fue sencilla. "Era la principal duda que teníamos. Son ocho horas de vuelo y otro continente completamente diferente. Pero la ciudad nos ha sorprendido mucho, vivimos muy tranquilos y el club nos ayuda en todo con un traductor para los jugadores extranjeros", explicó. Eso sí, el mayor desafío llega con los desplazamientos europeos. "Para jugar fuera tenemos que viajar dos días antes. Entre las seis o siete horas de vuelo y el cambio horario necesitas tiempo para adaptarte", concluyó un Marc Gual que ya suma un gol en Champions y tres tantos en la liga kazaja en sus primeras semanas con el Kairat.

articles.title: Cesc, el trampolín del Como: "Cuando llegué nos cambiábamos en un bar y ahora jugamos la Champions"
articles.standfirst: El entrenador español prepara una revolución para competir en Europa
articles.summary: El entrenador español prepara una revolución para competir en Europa
articles.body: El Como prepara el más difícil todavía. La victoria sobre la Cremonese (1-4) certificó la clasificación de los 'lariani' para la Champions por primera vez en su historia.  "Es un logro enorme, conseguido con jugadores jóvenes. El presidente me dio las riendas y tomé muchas decisiones. Cuando llegué hace cuatro años, como jugador, no teníamos centro de entrenamiento y nos cambiábamos en un bar. Ahora, en cambio, estamos en Champions", recordaba Cesc Fábregas. Un hito para el que ya han puesto las bases. “No se podía dar por sentado que uno de los mejores entrenadores de Europa, como Cesc, decidiera quedarse con nosotros en el Como, al igual que Nico Paz, uno de los mejores talentos del contiente”, reconoce el director deportivo, Carlalberto Ludi. Jugar en Europa implica una importante reforma a todos los niveles, empezando por el estadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia. No sólo se aumentará el aforo, también se ampliará el terreno de juego dos metros de ancho. La plantilla sufrirá un importante cambio. La Champions únicamente te permite disponer de 17 fichas libres —sin importar nacionalidad— en la lista A. El resto, hasta 25, sólo se puede completar con futbolistas formados en la Federación a la que perteneces. Esto supone un problema. El Como, la temporada pasada, sólo contaba con dos italianos en nómina: Vigorito y Goldaniga. Entre los dos jugaron 14 minutos en Serie A. “Fichar jugadores en Italia es un problema debido a la rigidez de los métodos de pago”, asegura el presidente Mirwan Suwarso, que ha pagado seis kilos al Cantanzaro por Liberali. “El sector juvenil es crucial. Debemos permitir que el talento crezca con paciencia”, subraya Cesc. Se han ido 'pesos pesados' (Diego Carlos, Sergi Roberto, Alberto Moreno...) y han seguido pescando en LaLiga: Luis Milla y Andrés Cuenca. Vendrán más. “Si no estás preparado para jugar en el Bernabéu o el Allianz, te arriesgas a encajar seis goles. Me gusta entrenar a jóvenes, pero debemos traer gente con experiencia”, insiste Cesc. La Champions le espera.

articles.title: A look at the most exciting moments from the 2026 FIFA World Cup
articles.summary: A photo gallery of highlights from World Cup 2026.
articles.body: The 2026 World Cup has come to a close. Spain is the winner after a thrilling 1-0 win in the final, holding off Lionel Messi and Argentina from winning a second consecutive title. The tournament began June 11 with the opening match in Mexico before play extended to the United States and Canada. It was an exciting tournament overall, as well as the first to feature 48 teams. New heroes — such as Cape Verde’s goalkeeper Vozinha — were created, while several of the sport’s legends — such as Messi and France’s Kylian Mbappé — continued putting their stamp on the world’s biggest stage. Here’s a look back at the tournament through some of the NBC News photo team’s favorite images, featuring unique atmospheres, raucous fans, the most memorable moments and more.

articles.title: El Fenerbahçe de Asensio golpea primero
articles.standfirst: Los 'canarios amarillos' ganan al Górnik Zabrze (1-0) en la ida de la 2ª ronda previa
articles.summary: Los 'canarios amarillos' ganan al Górnik Zabrze (1-0) en la ida de la 2ª ronda previa
articles.body: La Champions League sigue su curso. La disputa de la 2ª ronda previa ya está en marcha. Fenerbahçe, que debutaba, ha golpeado primero al derrotar por la mínima al Górnik Zabrze (1-0).  İsmail Kartal, que no pudo contar con Vedat Muriqi (lesionado) ni N'Golo Kanté, alineó de inicio al recién llegado Nathan Aké, sustituido al descanso. Se guardó, eso sí, varias 'cartas'. Ederson, Marco Asensio y Mason Greenwood comenzaron en el banquillo. El internacional español, que ultima su puesta a punto, saltó al campo en el 69' en sustitución de Bartug Elmaz. El gol del triunfo lo anotó Talisca en el 37' al transformar un libre directo con la zurda desde la frontal. El que tuvo un estreno triunfal como entrenador de Champions fue Yaya Touré. 'Su' Slovan Bratislava ganó 0-2 al Iberia 1999 gracias a los tantos de Andraz Sporar (25') y Alasana Yirajang (31'). El Dinamo Zagreb, por su parte, rescató un punto 'in extremis' ante el Thun (1-1) gracias al gol de Miha Zajc en el 86'. Sergi Domínguez fue titular, mientras que Raúl Torrente no jugó por lesión. Dani Rodríguez no figuraba en la convocatoria.   El Mjallby también encarriló su eliminatoria ante el Lincoln Red Imps (3-0) de Juanma Pavón, al igual que el Lech Poznan de Pablo Rodríguez (titular) frente al AGF (1-4). articles.title: La 'obra maestra' de Julio Velázquez: "Llegar a fase de grupos, aunque sea en Conference, sería un exitazo"
articles.standfirst: El estratega español aspira a seguir avanzando en Champions con 'su' Levski
articles.summary: El estratega español aspira a seguir avanzando en Champions con 'su' Levski
articles.body: Julio Velázquez (Salamanca, 1981) puso fin la temporada pasada a la mayor dinastía en activo del planeta fútbol, las 14 Ligas consecutivas que acumulaba el Ludogorets. “No siento que sea mi mayor obra. En los 29 años que llevo entrenando he vivido grandes momentos”, reconocía a MARCA. El exentrenador de Poli Ejido, Villarreal, Murcia, Betis, Alcorcón, Alavés y Zaragoza, entre otros, condujo al Levski a poner fin a ¡17 años! de sequía en Bulgaria. 'Novias' no le han faltado, pero se ha mantenido fiel al banquillo del Georgi Asparuhov. “Recibí diferentes opciones en distintos contextos que podían resultar atractivas tanto a nivel deportivo como económico, pero tengo contrato y me siento querido y valorado. Soy feliz y, aunque ya se ha conseguido hacer historia, pienso que todavía se puede serguir construyendo. Eso es algo bonito y atractivo”, afirma el técnico español. Consiguió superar al Ludogorets a pesar de tener un presupuesto cinco veces inferior y confía en repetir con un español en sus filas: Álex Centelles ha llegado libre del Almería. “El mercado es muy dinámico y dura muchísimo. Al empezar a competir en Europa tan pronto tenemos que estar atentos a posibles entradas y salidas. Las diferencias a nivel presupuestario siguen existiendo, pero mi responsabilidad es sacar el máximo rendimiento en base a las herramientas que tenemos a nuestra disposición”, subraya. Su Levski superó ampliamente al Borac Banja Luka (1-5) en su estreno en Champions. Ahora le espera el Universitatea Craiova... pero la posibilidad de jugar la Fase de Grupos de la Liga de Campeones por primera vez desde la 2006-07 sigue pareciendo lejana. “El equipo compitió muy bien en la 1ª ronda previa. Ahora tenemos un rival muy duro y debemosofrecer nuestra mejor versión. El Levski lleva casi 20 años sin jugar una fase de grupos de una competición europea. El año pasado estuvimos cerquita de lograrlo. Si esta temporada lo logramos, en cualquiera de las tres competiciones, sería un exitazo”, reivindica Julio Velázquez. El triunfo ante el Universitatea Craiova tendría un valor añadido: “Si pasamos una ronda más, sí que nos garantizaríamos jugar, como mínimo, la Fase de Grupos de la Conference, lo que ya sería algo absolutamente extraordinario. Vamos día a día con el objetivo de seguir compitiendo en Champions: los chicos se lo han merecido”. Una cosa tiene clara: lo que funciona no se toca. “La temporada pasada conseguimos romper la hegemonía del Ludogorets gracias al gran trabajo de los jugadores e intentamos, en cualquier competición, mantenernos fieles a nuestra identidad. Es decir, ser un equipo muy proactivo con y sin balón. En Europa debemos ajustar detalles para sentirnos cómodos y competir de una manera fiable, pero intentamos llevarlo a cabo”, insiste Julio Velázquez, que podría rubricar un 'cuadro' de Champions.

articles.title: Kvaratskhelia se aferra a la 'vía Kevin Keegan' para soñar con el Balón de Oro
articles.standfirst: El inglés fue el último futbolista que ganó el galardón en año de Mundial sin participar en el torneo
articles.summary: El inglés fue el último futbolista que ganó el galardón en año de Mundial sin participar en el torneo
articles.body: ¿hasta qué punto debe influir el torneo más importante del fútbol en la elección del Balón de Oro? Históricamente, la Copa del Mundo ha servido para impulsar candidaturas, pero no ha sido una garantía de éxito. De hecho, la propia organización del premio ha querido recordarlo una vez concluido el Mundial de 2026. En un artículo publicado tras la final, el Balón de Oro recuerda que, aunque conquistar la Copa del Mundo ayuda, no garantiza el premio. De hecho, desde que el galardón se abrió a futbolistas de todo el mundo en 1995, sólo cuatro de los siete ganadores en años de Mundial fueron también campeones del mundo. La conclusión del propio artículo es todavía más reveladora: “Para ganar el Balón de Oro hay que haber sido el mejor jugador de la temporada, no solo del Mundial”. Ese criterio vuelve a situar en la conversación a futbolistas como Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, ausente del Mundial pero autor de una de las temporadas más completas del fútbol europeo. El georgiano firmó una campaña sobresaliente con el Paris Saint-Germain, registrando 19 goles y 10 asistencias en 48 partidos, consolidándose como uno de los grandes líderes del campeón de Europa. Su candidatura al Balón de Oro se construyó, sobre todo, en la Champions League, competición en la que terminó con 10 goles y seis asistencias en 16 encuentros y fue elegido 'Mejor Jugador de la Temporada' de la UEFA Champions League. Desde el 'playoff' de acceso a los octavos de final frente al Mónaco hasta la final participó directamente en 10 goles (seis tantos y cuatro asistencias). Además, en la final provocó el penalti que permitió al PSG igualar el encuentro antes de conquistar la primera Champions League de su historia. Y existe un precedente histórico que refuerza esa misma idea. En 1978, en pleno año de Mundial, Kevin Keegan conquistó el Balón de Oro después de una extraordinaria temporada con el Hamburgo, a pesar de que Inglaterra ni siquiera se había clasificado para la Copa del Mundo. Casi medio siglo después, la reflexión vuelve a ser la misma: si el Balón de Oro debe reconocer al mejor futbolista de toda la temporada, y no únicamente al más brillante del Mundial, la candidatura de Khvicha Kvaratskhelia mantiene argumentos más que suficientes para seguir entre las grandes favoritas al galardón.

articles.title: Yaya Touré, un estreno de Champions: "Los jugadores son las estrellas"
articles.standfirst: El exjugador del Barcelona debutó como entrenador del Slovan Bratislava en la previa
articles.summary: El exjugador del Barcelona debutó como entrenador del Slovan Bratislava en la previa
articles.body: Yaya Touré (Bouaké, 1983) llevaba tiempo preparándose para dar el salto a los banquillos. Ejerció de asistente en Olimpik Donetsk, Akhmat Grozny y Standard antes de convertirse en la 'mano derecha' de Roberto Mancini en Arabia Saudí.   Ahora, tras hacer sus 'pinitos' en la Academia del Tottenham, afronta su primera aventura en solitario como entrenador del Slovan Bratislava. "Mi objetivo era traer a una persona y una personalidad que haya vivido el mejor fútbol del mundo. Me causó una impresión maravillosa: tiene un gran deseo y motivación para triunfar como entrenador", reconocía Ivan Kmotrík Jr., director general del club.  "He tenido la oportunidad de trabajar con entrenadores excelentes en el pasado, pero anhelaba crear mi propio proyecto. Tengo mucho que aprender. Soy consciente de mis limitaciones", apunta el marfileño, que ha 'pasó por las manos' de Guardiola, Pellegrini, Mancini, Rijkaard... El ex de Barcelona, Manchester City, Mónaco y Olympiacos, entre otros, 'aparca' los más de 700 partidos, 127 goles, 73 asistencias y 18 títulos que coleccionó a lo largo de su carrera como jugador: "Lo tengo claro. Los jugadores son las estrellas. Están en el campo y han ganado las últimas ocho Ligas de forma consecutiva; es a los que todos miran".  La propuesta, eso sí, es innegociable. "Quiero que dominemos el juego y seamos agresivos cuando no tengamos la posesión. Nuestro principal objetivo debe ser marcar goles. No soy el tipo de entrenador que se toma los partidos con cautela: soy un ganador y me encanta ganar", confesaba a 'Dennik Sport'. Su estreno oficial llegó a lo grande, en Champions. El Slovan Bratislava de Yaya Touré -su hermano Kolo fue ayudante de Guardiola en el Manchester City- debutó con victoria sobre el Iberia 1999 (0-2) en la ida de la segunda ronda previa. "La actitud de los jugadores fue excelente. Estoy satisfecho, trabajamos bien, pero todavía tenemos margen de mejora. Hay que entender que este es un proceso que llevará tiempo. articles.title: El Fermín más tocado: "Ha sido el peor verano de mi vida"
articles.standfirst: El atacante del Barça reconoce que ha necesitado ayuda y que su coach personal ha tenido trabajo extra para ayudarle a salir adelante
articles.summary: El atacante del Barça reconoce que ha necesitado ayuda y que su coach personal ha tenido trabajo extra para ayudarle a salir adelante
articles.body: "Ha sido el peor verano de mi vida. Estaba en el mejor momento, todo salía bien y llegó la lesión. También se aprende de estas situaciones, pero es cierto que este verano lo he pasado muy mal.   He salido adelante gracias a mi familia, mi compañera y mis amigos. He necesitado ayuda. Ya tenía antes, pero mi coach me ha ayudado mucho a salir adelante", las palabras de Fermín en el programa a Tot Costa de Catalunya Ràdio desde el stage de pretemporada del Barça en Inglaterra son definitorias.  Fermín reconoce en la entrevista que los primeros partidos de España se los tuvo que ahorrar. "Los primeros partidos de la selección española en el Mundial no los vi. No podía. Quería estar allí en el Mundial. Que quede claro que me ha hecho muy feliz ver a mis compañeros ganar el Mundial. En el tramo final del Mundial ya lo pasé algo mejor y decidí ir a ver la final en directo a Nueva York". "Me encuentro cada día mejor. No tengo molestias, que es importante. Si todo va bien, en el Gámper podría jugar ya unos minutos. La intención es volver de esa lesión con más motivación. Creo que estoy muy preparado. Ya he demostrado cómo puedo ayudar al Barça y esta próxima temporada tengo que seguir igual". "El sueño de la Champions es compartido con todo el equipo. Los dos últimos años hemos estado cerca. Esta temporada puede ser buena. Llevamos tres años jugando juntos y hemos vivido muchas cosas. Siento que estamos preparados para ganar la Champions. Ganar la tercera liga consecutiva es difícil. Será un año complicado. Pero si nosotros estamos centrados en nuestro juego y estamos unidos podemos ganar la tercera liga".

articles.title: Yahoo Fantasy Death Leagues 101: How to play and win in this exciting format
articles.summary: Death Leagues are back on Yahoo fantasy football. Here's the 101.
articles.body:
We're thrilled to start another season of Yahoo Fantasy Death Leagues for 2026 . In this killer fantasy football game, fans compete for survival every week.

Create a private Death League or join a public one for the 2026 NFL season

Death Leagues offer a different approach from most fantasy leagues by removing the head-to-head matchups and replacing them with a weekly battle royale between all managers, where the team with the lowest total score for that week is eliminated.

To make things even more interesting, the entire roster of players from the team that gets knocked out goes to the waiver wire — where everyone will have a chance to bid on them.

That process continues week after week until one team is left standing and that lone surviving manager is crowned the winner.

To put it simply, Death Leagues combine the best parts of fantasy drafting and waiver wire adds, with an undeniable urgency to survive every single week. Instead of trying to win against one opponent, your goal is to avoid being the worst team in the league each week in order to escape elimination.

As long as you're not at the very bottom, you keep playing.

For private leagues, the default is 18 teams vying for the title, ending in Week 17. Private leagues can decide how many teams to play with and when to start. Public leagues consist of 14 teams and will play for 13 weeks.

However, you can begin a Death League with as few as four teams. Just know that fewer teams means a shorter fantasy season for your league.

And if you don't set your draft up before Week 1 — no worries! You can start your league anytime up until Week 15.

What are the lineup and rosters requirements?

While there are a lot of differences between season-long fantasy football leagues and Death League formats, this is one area where you'll feel right at home.

Here's a closer look at the roster breakdown:

One thing to note is that Death Leagues tend to feature more teams, as long as you start early in the year. This is important because there's a big difference in the players available during the later rounds of a 12-team league versus an 18-teamer.

So if you're starting in Week 1, keep that in mind when you're looking at your roster in the opening month. At that point in the season, everyone has question marks in their lineups.

This is another area that will be very familiar to fantasy managers, since the scoring settings are the same as you would have in many other formats.

-Fewest cumulative -Fewest points from a starter, 2nd, 3rd, etc.

-Fewest points from a starter, 2nd, 3rd, etc.

As always, make sure you go over the scoring before you draft so that you're well prepared to take players that fit this format.

Now, here's where strategy comes into play even more.

All managers will begin the season with $1,000 and you'll make a decision on how much of that budget you want to put towards acquiring a specific player before waivers are processed.

But the biggest difference between traditional fantasy leagues and the Death League format is the quality of free agents available each week. For example, if the team with Ja'Marr Chase finished last in Week 1 — then Chase will be up for grabs on the waiver wire before Week 2.

By the end of the season, the remaining teams will be completely stacked with stars, which means the incoming crop of players from the losing roster will be that much more impressive every week.

So, it's important to make sure you save some FAB for the stretch run if you hope to finish the season as the champion.

What are some general strategies for Death Leagues?

Navigating the nuances of Death Leagues offers a new challenge for fantasy managers.

We'll go over some of the specific strategies with more detail in other articles, but here's a quick look at some of the approaches you'll want to consider for this format.

Since your main goal is to make it through each week, most of your focus needs to be on the present. If you look too far ahead, you could find yourself eliminated from the league before you even make it to those future scenarios.

You'll also have plenty of opportunities to bolster your roster through the waiver wire as the season progresses, thanks to the higher quality free agents who will become available on a weekly basis. So, don't worry about the later stages of the campaign until you get closer to it.

Get ready for Yahoo Fantasy Death Leagues

While traditional redraft leagues reward chasing upside, Death League formats give a boost in value to players with high floors who can be trusted to give you steady production — even if they don't offer a massive fantasy ceiling.

This is especially true in the early part of the season, when there will be lots of teams that will be on the verge of getting eliminated because one or two of their stars had a bad week. It might feel odd, but trusting stable, high-floor veterans can be the difference between advancing or going home in the first couple months.

Projecting fantasy strength of schedule can be a dangerous game, since so much can change over the course of an NFL season. Narrowing your focus to the early part of the campaign has always been the best use of strength of schedule and that's even more important in Death Leagues.

If you draft a star player who has a tough string of opponents in the first few weeks , their production might be underwhelming and your season might come to an early end. On the flip side, if a player has a softer slate in September they might provide more value than other managers realize. So, keep a close eye on the early matchups for the players you're drafting.

Early bye weeks can be an insurmountable obstacle for your lineup, if you don't factor them into your build. Stars with early byes lose some of their value in this format and often end up on the waiver wire after those weeks because their managers get eliminated.

You also want to pay close attention so you don't have too many players on bye during the same week in the first half of the season. Having players on bye in the second half of the year is also not ideal, but you'll have plenty of time to change your roster before those problem weeks arrive.

Balancing the risk/reward for volatile fantasy options is a key part of most redraft leagues. Seeing past red flags and hitting on the right player could change your season.

However, in Death Leagues, that is a much more dangerous proposition. Avoiding risk at the start of the season is usually the much better approach.

An injury to a high-end running back could decimate your lineup in Death Leagues, so insulating your backfield against potential injuries is a more useful plan in this format.

If you're going to take a running back in the early rounds, keep their backup on your radar in the later rounds of drafts — or at worst on your watchlist if they go undrafted.

With so many teams with varying levels of success throughout the season, the desperation is real when it comes to the waiver wire.

If a manager just barely avoided last place the week before, you can be sure their bids will be aggressive in an attempt to vault themselves away from the danger zone. Try to look at your leaguemates' rosters to get a feel for how they might attack their bids that week.

While the excitement of seeing superstar names on the waiver wire might make you want to do everything in your power to add them, you have to remember it's a long season in Death Leagues.

If you don't save some of your budget for the final stretch, you'll be powerless against opponents who still have money in the bank when the player pool is loaded near the end.

If you survive long enough, your team will be stacked and there will be plenty of talent available. When you get to the point where every remaining roster is brimming with stars, you'll want to make sure to increase your focus on matchups again.

Just because a player is a household name, doesn't necessarily mean they're in the best position to keep you alive in the final month. Your path to a title may very well come down to which star capitalizes on a generous defense in a given week.

As the season goes along, you'll get a sense of how your team compares to other rosters in the league. While you might be able to wait things out in more typical redraft leagues, you cannot take that risk in Death Leagues. You have to address weaknesses as soon as you identify them.

If you find your team is coasting near the top early in the season, then you can take advantage and plan a little bit further ahead than your opponents in an effort to set yourself up for the long haul towards a Death League championship.

articles.title: Liverpool: Key questions answered as Amit Bhatia, Jeff Bezos and Eduardo Saverin agree purchase of strategic minority stake
articles.summary: Amazon founder Jeff Bezos is part of the Amit Bhatia-led consortium that has agreed to buy a stake in Liverpool; Sky News reports the group are buying around one third of the Reds in a deal valuing the club at more than $7bn (£5.2bn); we take a deep dive into what the deal could mean
articles.body:
Liverpool's owners Fenway Sports Group have sold a stake in Liverpool Football Club to a consortium including Amazon founder Jeff Bezos.

The world's third richest person is part of the group fronted by former QPR co-owner Amit Bhatia. Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin is also part of the syndicate.

According to Sky News, the consortium has agreed to buy a roughly one-third stake in the club in a deal that values Liverpool at more than $7bn (£5.2bn). Closing of the transaction is subject to regulatory approvals and other customary closing conditions.

We take a look at some of the key questions surrounding what the deal could look like...

What are the details?

The Bezos-backed consortium bought a 38 per cent stake in Liverpool from FSG.

It was initially suggested by sources close to the deal that the investment was for 30-33 per cent of the Premier League club.

However, Sky Sports News can confirm that 1892 Holdings has bought a stake closer to 40 per cent in Liverpool.

Sky Sports News reported last week that Liverpool's new minority investors have an option to become majority shareholders of the Premier League club.

According to Sky's US partner CNBC, this option is active for 12 months and would value Liverpool at around $8bn.

Sources have stressed the existence of such an agreement is not a guarantee of any future transaction.

Liverpool's statement last week said FSG continues to retain majority ownership and operational control of the club.

Who are Bezos and Bhatia?

Bezos is one of the most famous businessmen in the world and the owner of e-commerce giant Amazon, which he founded in 1994 out of his Seattle garage.

His other investments include aerospace company Blue Origin and venture capital firm Nash Holdings, which is the ownership vehicle for The Washington Post.

Bhatia is a 46-year-old British Indian entrepreneur, who has an investment banking background.

He currently manages a multi-asset investment firm called AyBe Capital which invests in range of diversified sectors including technology, media, property and real estate, consumer retail and health.

Bhatia is married to Vanisha Mittal Bhatia, who is the daughter of Indian billionaire Lakshmi Mittal.

He leads and manages 1892 Holdings, the consortium that has agreed the minority investment in Liverpool with majority owners Fenway Sports Group.

  • Transfer Centre LIVE! | Liverpool news & transfers 🔴
  • Got Sky? Watch Liverpool games LIVE on your phone📱
  • Not got Sky? Get Sky Sports or stream with no contract on NOW📺
  • Choose the Sky Sports push notifications you want! 🔔

What are they worth?

Forbes estimates that Bezos' personal fortune is in the region of $281bn (£209bn), making him the third-richest person in the world behind Elon Musk and Google co-founder Larry Page.

It's unclear how much Bhatia himself is worth. But his father-in-law, billionaire steel magnate Lakshmi Mittal, is worth an estimated £23.2bn according to Forbes. That makes him the 72nd richest person in the world.

What are their sporting interests?

Bezos is a big American Football fan and has previously been reported to have explored bids for the Washington Commanders and the Seattle Seahawks.

He is not known to hold a significant stake in any other sports team or enterprise currently.

Bhatia was just 28 when he joined the board of directors and became vice-chairman of QPR in 2007 after the Mittal family bought a 20 per cent stake in QPR, joining Bernie Ecclestone and Flavio Briatore as investors in the London club.

He spent five years as QPR chairman between 2018 and 2023 and stayed on as a director and co-owner until earlier this week when he transferred his stake in the club to majority owner Ruben Gnanalingam.

Through AyBe capital, Bhatia is an investor in TGL - Rory McIlroy and Tiger Woods' golf league which fuses golf and technology and features six teams with some of the best players in the world in a season-long competition.

His firm also invests in Switch Hitter, which is a media brand founded by Kevin Pietersen, delivering exclusive interviews and content with the world's top cricketers.

Earlier this year, Bhatia's father-in-law acquired a 75 per cent stake in the Rajasthan Royals Indian Premier League cricket franchise.

Why have FSG decided to sell?

FSG were under no pressure to sell but did indicate in 2022 that they were open to new investment in Liverpool, with the sale of a small stake to Dynasty Equity completed the following year.

Liverpool have enjoyed huge success under FSG, lifting every major trophy available to win.

FSG may think it is mission accomplished somewhat as far they are concerned, and therefore were amenable to fresh investment. They also stand to make a huge profit on their initial investment, with the deal for a 30 per cent stake worth more than five times what they paid for the entire club back in 2010.

Could the Bezos-backed group take over Liverpool?

Liverpool's new minority investors have an option to become majority shareholders of the Premier League club for a valuation of around $8bn in the next 12 months, according to Sky's US partner CNBC.

Sky Sports News has been told the agreement announced today includes a framework for future investment from the Jeff Bezos-backed consortium.

However, sources have stressed that the existence of such an agreement is not a guarantee of any future transaction.

Liverpool's statement says FSG continues to retain majority ownership and operational control of the club.

What is the club valued at?

Liverpool are the fourth most valuable club in the world. The consortium's investment in Liverpool values the club somewhere in the region of £5.2bn ($7bn), making it one of the sport's richest-ever deals.

Who owns Liverpool?

FSG have complete operational control of Liverpool, but private equity firms RedBird Capital and Arctos Sports Partners hold minority stakes in the club. Dynasty Equity are also passive investors in Liverpool after injecting £164m into the club in 2023 in a deal valuing Liverpool at more than $4.5bn.

How much did FSG pay for Liverpool?

FSG were known as New England Sports Ventures when they paid £300m for Liverpool in October 2010 after a tumultuous period under former owners Tom Hicks and George Gillett.

When will the deal go through?

The deal - which was first reported on at the end of last month - has accelerated at a rapid pace. Now that everything has been agreed, the closing of the transaction will happen after regulatory approvals and other customary closing conditions are met.

Who else is involved?

Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin and his wife Elaine are also part of the syndicate of investors. Saverin, 44, was part of a consortium which assembled an unsuccessful takeover bid for Chelsea during the 2022 auction triggered by Vladimir Putin's invasion of Ukraine.

Bhatia is married to Vanisha Mittal Bhatia, who is the daughter of Indian billionaire Lakshmi Mittal.

He leads and manages 1892 Holdings, the consortium that has agreed the minority investment in Liverpool with majority owners Fenway Sports Group.

What are they worth?

Forbes estimates that Bezos' personal fortune is in the region of $281bn (£209bn), making him the third-richest person in the world behind Elon Musk and Google co-founder Larry Page.

It's unclear how much Bhatia himself is worth. But his father-in-law, billionaire steel magnate Lakshmi Mittal, is worth an estimated £23.2bn according to Forbes. That makes him the 72nd richest person in the world.

What are their sporting interests?

Bezos is a big American Football fan and has previously been reported to have explored bids for the Washington Commanders and the Seattle Seahawks.

He is not known to hold a significant stake in any other sports team or enterprise currently.

Bhatia was just 28 when he joined the board of directors and became vice-chairman of QPR in 2007 after the Mittal family bought a 20 per cent stake in QPR, joining Bernie Ecclestone and Flavio Briatore as investors in the London club.

He spent five years as QPR chairman between 2018 and 2023 and stayed on as a director and co-owner until earlier this week when he transferred his stake in the club to majority owner Ruben Gnanalingam.

Through AyBe capital, Bhatia is an investor in TGL - Rory McIlroy and Tiger Woods' golf league which fuses golf and technology and features six teams with some of the best players in the world in a season-long competition.

His firm also invests in Switch Hitter, which is a media brand founded by Kevin Pietersen, delivering exclusive interviews and content with the world's top cricketers.

Earlier this year, Bhatia's father-in-law acquired a 75 per cent stake in the Rajasthan Royals Indian Premier League cricket franchise.

Why have FSG decided to sell?

FSG were under no pressure to sell but did indicate in 2022 that they were open to new investment in Liverpool, with the sale of a small stake to Dynasty Equity completed the following year.

Liverpool have enjoyed huge success under FSG, lifting every major trophy available to win.

FSG may think it is mission accomplished somewhat as far they are concerned, and therefore were amenable to fresh investment. They also stand to make a huge profit on their initial investment, with the deal for a 30 per cent stake worth more than five times what they paid for the entire club back in 2010.

Could the Bezos-backed group take over Liverpool?

Liverpool's new minority investors have an option to become majority shareholders of the Premier League club for a valuation of around $8bn in the next 12 months, according to Sky's US partner CNBC.

Sky Sports News has been told the agreement announced today includes a framework for future investment from the Jeff Bezos-backed consortium.

However, sources have stressed that the existence of such an agreement is not a guarantee of any future transaction.

Liverpool's statement says FSG continues to retain majority ownership and operational control of the club.

What is the club valued at?

Liverpool are the fourth most valuable club in the world. The consortium's investment in Liverpool values the club somewhere in the region of £5.2bn ($7bn), making it one of the sport's richest-ever deals.

Who owns Liverpool?

FSG have complete operational control of Liverpool, but private equity firms RedBird Capital and Arctos Sports Partners hold minority stakes in the club. Dynasty Equity are also passive investors in Liverpool after injecting £164m into the club in 2023 in a deal valuing Liverpool at more than $4.5bn.

How much did FSG pay for Liverpool?

FSG were known as New England Sports Ventures when they paid £300m for Liverpool in October 2010 after a tumultuous period under former owners Tom Hicks and George Gillett.

When will the deal go through?

The deal - which was first reported on at the end of last month - has accelerated at a rapid pace. Now that everything has been agreed, the closing of the transaction will happen after regulatory approvals and other customary closing conditions are met.

Who else is involved?

Facebook co-founder Eduardo Saverin and his wife Elaine are also part of the syndicate of investors. Saverin, 44, was part of a consortium which assembled an unsuccessful takeover bid for Chelsea during the 2022 auction triggered by Vladimir Putin's invasion of Ukraine.

articles.title: Heisman Candidate LaNorris Sellers Interning at Local Driving Range During Fall Semester
articles.summary: When he's not on a football field this fall, you might find South Carolina quarterback LaNorris Sellers on the range.
articles.body:
When he's not on a football field this fall, you might find South Carolina quarterback LaNorris Sellers on the range.

According to Hale McGranahan of Gamecock247, Sellers is interning The Par Tee Golf Center in West Columbia, South Carolina. It's the only college coursework he has to worry about for the time being as he has no classes on his academic schedule.

Sellers is majoring in sport and entertainment management, and he's on his way toward graduating in December.

A previous internship took him to Contract Construction, the South Carolina-based company that's working on the renovations to Williams-Brice Stadium.

"I sat in with a lot of those meetings at the stadium, the group out of Oklahoma that they gave the job to build the stadium, do the design and all that, I met with them," Sellers said of his time there. "I pretty much knew what was going on over there before a lot of people did."

His tasks at Par Tee are far more menial. He told McGrahanan he mostly performs "facility management," such as mowing the grass and picking up golf balls.

While he's out on the range, Sellers presumably takes the chance to mentally go over the Gamecocks' offensive scheme or think about areas of his own game to improve.

South Carolina didn't make the Associated Press Top 25 poll , but challenging for the College Football Playoff isn't out of the question .

A lot will hinge on the performance of Sellers, who threw for 2,437 yards, 13 touchdowns and eight interceptions in 2025.

His individual tools are off the charts . If he puts together a big year, he could enter the Heisman Trophy conversation and perhaps climb into the first round on 2027 NFL draft boards.

articles.title: Dylan Stewart Injury Update, Latest on Potential Top-10 NFL Draft Pick Before South Carolina Opener
articles.summary: South Carolina head coach Shane Beamer revealed that it's unrealistic to think pass-rusher Dylan Stewart will be ready for the beginning of the 2026 season, per Lulu Kesin of the Greenville News.
articles.body:
South Carolina head coach Shane Beamer revealed that it's unrealistic to think pass-rusher Dylan Stewart will be ready for the beginning of the 2026 season, per Lulu Kesin of the Greenville News .

On3.com's Chris Low also reported that Stewart and offensive tackle Jacarrius Peak were unlikely to suit up in the Gamecocks' season-opener on Sept. 5.

Expectations are high for the 20-year-old Stewart, as he was projected to be selected with the No. 9 overall pick in the latest 2027 mock draft from Bleacher Report's NFL Scouting Department.

Stewart has continued to deal with a back injury that he suffered during the 2025 season.

While he still appeared in 11 of South Carolina's 12 games last year, he missed all of the team's spring practices while recovering from the back issue.

Beamer previously gave an update on Stewart's injury in April.

"Continue to just get well with his injury. It's one of those that just needs rest right now," Beamer said at the time, per On3.com's Jack Veltri . "Kind of the same thing I told you guys a few weeks ago. He just needs to rest. It's not like we send him to a doctor, and he makes a couple of adjustments and he's good to go and he jumps right back into the weight room. He just needs to rest. That's the plan for him right now."

Stewart was productive despite playing through the injury last season, finishing with 33 tackles and 12 tackles for loss to go along with 4.5 sacks. He also amassed three forced fumbles and two passes defended.

South Carolina will open its 2026 campaign against Kent State on Sept. 5.

articles.title: Tennessee Reveals 'Neyland Legacy' Uniforms in New Video, Photos for 2026 CFB Season
articles.summary: Having already named their home stadium after Hall of Fame head coach Robert Neyland, the Tennessee Volunteers are incorporating his legacy into their uniforms for the 2026 season.
articles.body:
Having already named their home stadium after Hall of Fame head coach Robert Neyland, the Tennessee Volunteers are incorporating his legacy into their uniforms for the 2026 season.

The Vols revealed the "Neyland Legacy" uniforms they will add to their rotation for the upcoming season.

Some of the Neyland-specific aspects of the design include a patch on the left shoulder in the image of him kneeling, similar to the Neyland statue that sits outside of their home stadium.

The helmet design is based off the leather model the Vols used in the very-early days of the football program.

Neyland spent a total of 21 seasons as Tennessee's head coach across three different stints between 1926 to '52. He also had multiple stints in the military as a member of the Army, including in 1941 during World War II.

Tennessee went 173-31-12 and won four national titles during Neyland's tenure. He was inducted into the College Football Hall of Fame in 1956.

The Volunteers will kickoff the 2026 season at Neyland Stadium against Furman on Sept. 5 at 3:30 p.m. ET.

articles.title: Penn State QB Rocco Becht Reveals on Video He's Unsure What Class He Will Take After ISU Transfer
articles.summary: Penn State quarterback Rocco Becht revealed that he hasn't determined the class he'll take during the fall semester after transferring to the Nittany Lions from Iowa State.
articles.body:
Penn State quarterback Rocco Becht revealed that he hasn't determined the class he'll take during the fall semester after transferring to the Nittany Lions from Iowa State.

"I don't know yet, we haven't picked it yet," Becht told reporters Thursday (0:35 mark). "So, we've gotta do that here coming up this weekend for school to start next week. Yeah, I'm in one class. I guess it's the props of being graduated and being a fifth-year."

The 22-year-old graduated from Iowa State with a degree in communication studies in Dec. 2025 before transferring.

Becht still had one year of eligibility remaining, as he redshirted for the Cyclones in 2022.

He went on to serve as Iowa State's starting quarterback from 2023-25, throwing for 9,209 yards and 64 touchdowns across that span.

During the 2025 season, Becht completed 60.5 percent of his passes for 2,584 yards and 16 touchdowns while getting picked off nine times in 12 games. He helped the Cyclones finish with a record of 8-4.

Becht has now reunited with head coach Matt Campbell in Happy Valley, as Campbell previously coached him throughout his tenure at Iowa State before he was hired by Penn State as James Franklin's full-time replacement.

Becht was one of 24 former Cyclones players to follow Campbell to the Nittany Lions in the transfer portal (h/t 247Sports' Tyler Donohue ).

While Penn State is coming off a disappointing 7-6 finish in 2025, the team is still looking to climb up the Big Ten standings next season. The school was listed at No. 18 in the preseason Associated Press Top 25 .

As Becht prepares to start under center, he has yet to pick out his lone class for the upcoming semester.

articles.title: 'College GameDay' to Broadcast from Ole Miss for Lane Kiffin's Return with LSU in Week 3
articles.summary: College GameDay is heading to Mississippi for what could be the most-anticipated game of the 2026 college football regular season.
articles.body:
College GameDay is heading to Mississippi for what could be the most-anticipated game of the 2026 college football regular season.

ESPN announced on Friday that the signature college football pre-game show will be at the University of Mississippi on Sept. 19 for Lane Kiffin's return to Oxford when the Rebels host LSU.

Kiffin's debut season with the Tigers is making LSU an appealing option for ESPN. College Gameday will be in Baton Rouge for his first home game against Clemson on Sept. 5.

In between Kiffin games, ESPN will send the Gameday crew to Austin on Sept. 12 for Ohio State vs. Texas.

Kiffin left Ole Miss to take the LSU job on Nov. 30, leaving the Rebels to play in the College Football Playoff with Pete Golding taking over as head coach.

Mississippi went 55-19 in six seasons with Kiffin as head coach from 2020 to '25.

articles.title: Nick Saban Says Alabama 'Could Sneak Up on People' in 2026, Hypes Georgia, Texas for CFP Runs
articles.summary: Legendary former Alabama head coach Nick Saban believes that the Crimson Tide can exceed expectations during the 2026 college football season.
articles.body:
Legendary former Alabama head coach Nick Saban believes that the Crimson Tide can exceed expectations during the 2026 college football season.

Saban said that Alabama was "under-the-radar" and "may be able to sneak up on people" during a Friday appearance on the Pat McAfee Show (0:47 mark).

He also discussed the College Football Playoff outlook for Georgia and head coach Kirby Smart as well as Texas and head coach Steve Sarkisian.

"I talked to Kirby and Sark both and I think both of those guys have really, really good teams," Saban said (0:27 mark). "I think they're probably the two teams that, at least on paper looking at this season, probably have the best chance to be successful and maybe go a long way in the playoff."

Alabama is coming off a CFP quarterfinal appearance last season, finishing with an 11-4 record under head coach Kalen DeBoer.

The Crimson Tide still boast one of the country's top secondaries, owning the SEC's No. 1 pass defense in 2025 by allowing a mere 169.9 yards per game through the air.

While quarterback Ty Simpson is no longer in the mix after he was selected in the 2026 NFL draft, Keelon Russell and Austin Mack are battling to start under center for Alabama.

Georgia is attempting to clinch a third consecutive CFP berth this year after ranking No. 3 in the preseason Associated Press Top 25 .

Although there's some uncertainty surrounding the Bulldogs' receiving corps following the departures of Zachariah Branch and Colbie Young, Smart's squad still contains plenty of talent.

Texas closed its 2025 campaign on a high note and finished at 10-3, but missed the CFP.

The Longhorns are once again led by Arch Manning at quarterback and brought in a transfer portal class that ranked No. 3 in the country, per 247Sports .

Texas sat at No. 5 in the preseason AP Top 25 poll.

articles.title: Lionel Messi Fined After Hitting Quinn Sullivan During Inter Miami vs. Philadelphia Union Fight
articles.summary: Lionel Messi avoided a suspension, but he was reportedly fined an undisclosed amount after he slapped Philadelphia Union forward Quinn Sullivan in the back of the head during Wednesday's 2-2 draw.
articles.body:
Lionel Messi avoided a suspension, but he was reportedly fined an undisclosed amount after he slapped Philadelphia Union forward Quinn Sullivan in the back of the head during Wednesday's 2-2 draw.

The Associated Press reported Messi and Inter Miami defender Ian Fray were each fined an undisclosed amount of money for different incidents in the contest.

Fray was fined for grabbing Sullivan's neck when they got tangled in the penalty area. Sullivan responded by tackling Fray.

Those weren't the only incidents in the heated game, as Cavan Sullivan and Yannick Bright each received red cards at the end of the contest for their scuffle:

However, insider Glenn Crooks reported Sullivan's red card was rescinded upon further review, which means he will be allowed to play in Saturday's contest against Austin.

Messi was a major storyline during the game for more than his back-and-forth with Sullivan. He buried a goal in the 26th minute, which gave Inter Miami a 2-1 advantage. Yet Philadelphia battled back to earn the draw and the point that came with it thanks to a second-half goal from Neil Pierre.

It was the second game between Miami and Philadelphia this season, and both featured dramatics.

While Wednesday's was defined more by the scuffles and fights outside the actual soccer, their matchup in May was more about the on-field fireworks. The two sides combined for 10 goals, eight of which came in the first half, on the way to Miami's 6-4 victory.

They will not face each other again this season unless they match up in the playoffs.

That would require a dramatic turnaround for Philadelphia, which is in 13th place in the Eastern Conference with 20 points. Inter Miami is well on its way to the playoffs in second place with 39 points.

articles.title: Portuguese Soccer Player Quévin Castro, 25, Dies After Playing in Friendly Match
articles.summary: MALVEIRA, Portugal (AP) — Portuguese soccer player Quévin Castro has died after collapsing during a friendly match playing for fourth-division team Real Sport Clube. He was 25.
articles.body:
MALVEIRA, Portugal (AP) — Portuguese soccer player Quévin Castro has died after collapsing during a friendly match playing for fourth-division team Real Sport Clube. He was 25.

The Lisbon Football Association and his club announced Castro's death on Saturday, saying he died during a preseason match earlier in the day against Estrela de Amadora at the Estádio das Seixas stadium in Malveira.

"Quevin Castro was far more than a player, he was a member of our family, leaving a mark on all those who had the privilege of knowing him, both on and off the pitch," Real Sport Clube said in a social media post.

Live All the Action: Fulham vs. Chelsea 🔥

Castro's former club West Bromwich Albion in England said it was "devastated" to learn of Castro's "untimely passing," and announced it will pay tribute with a period of applause in the 25th minute in its game against Burnley on Sunday, when the players will also wear black armbands.

"Quevin joined the Baggies as a teenager in 2021 and went on to make his first-team debut in a Carabao Cup tie against Arsenal," the club said. "He made his maiden league outing for the club in February 2022 and later had loan spells at Burton, Notts County and Gateshead, before departing The Hawthorns in the summer of 2023.

"After leaving Albion, Quevin spent time at York City, King's Lynn, Chippenham, Cambridge City and Eastbourne, before returning to his native Portugal."

articles.title: Jules Ahoka: Sunderland sign midfielder from Royal Antwerp
articles.summary: Sunderland confirm the signing of midfielder Jules Ahoka for a 10m euros (Â£8.6m) fee.
articles.body:
Sunderland have signed midfielder Jules Ahoka from Belgian side Royal Antwerp for 10m euros (Â£8.6m).

The Black Cats said the 20-year-old DR Congo youth international has signed a long-term contract with the club.

"I am very happy and proud to join Sunderland ," said Ahoka, who featured in both of Antwerp's league games this season.

"It is a big club with great ambitions, and I am excited to be here.

"I want to work hard, learn from my team-mates and the staff, and continue developing as a player. I will give everything for the club and I cannot wait to get started."

Ahoka becomes the Black Cats' third summer signing, following the arrival of Belgian left-back Thomas Meunier and French right-back Dayann Methalie.

"Jules is a player we have been following closely and he has shown some very encouraging qualities for his age," said Sunderland director of football Florent Ghisolfi.

"He has huge potential and we believe Sunderland is the right environment for him to continue his development."

Sunderland were beaten 2-1 by Ipswich in their Premier League opener on Saturday. Their next match is against Fulham on Sunday (14:00 BST).

articles.title: Lane Kiffin Denies Calling Browns' Todd Monken While Recruiting Dae'Quan Wright to LSU
articles.summary: Cleveland Browns head coach Todd Monken claimed that Lane Kiffin called him to ask about Dae'Quan Wright, but the LSU head coach denied that claim on Monday.
articles.body:
Cleveland Browns head coach Todd Monken claimed that Lane Kiffin called him to ask about Dae'Quan Wright, but the LSU head coach denied that claim on Monday.

"There's some inaccuracies in that story, but I don't know," Kiffin said. "Maybe someone else called him that said they were me. I actually don't know Todd. I guess somebody left him a text or called him that was me, cause I don't know him or have his number."

Wright, 22, went undrafted in the 2026 NFL draft and joined the Philadelphia Eagles before being claimed off waivers by the Browns earlier this month. Cleveland released him on Monday, and his agents say he will join LSU if he clears waivers.

Monken said in his availability last week that as far as he knew, Wright had a medical issue that "wasn't allowing him to practice" and that the decision to release him had "nothing to do with me."

Monken also said Kiffin had called him, but he didn't return the call.

"I wondered why Lane Kiffin reached out a week ago. Now I know," Monken said. "S--t, I didn't know, now I know. I didn't call him back, guess I should've"

Wright is believed to be the first player to reach an agreement to return to the collegiate level after being signed by an NFL team as an undrafted free agent. The move also would reunite Wright with his former coach.

The tight end spent the first two years of his college career with Virginia Tech before playing for Ole Miss in 2024 and 2025. Last season, he had 635 yards and five touchdowns.

Wright is one of several college football players fighting for another year of eligibility after the NCAA passed new eligibility rules that give athletes a five-year window to play at the college level.

Louisiana's 19th Judicial District Court passed a temporary restraining order last week that would allow more than 30 college athletes and 16 former college football players to play another year. Several of those players, like Wright, are on NFL training camp rosters.

Jack Pyburn, a former LSU linebacker who is currently with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers, could also join the Wright, Kiffin and the Tigers this season.

Whether Kiffin is actually recruiting NFL players is another question that could open a new can of worms, but he claims not to have reached out to Monken.
